newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey seeks $750-800 million of sell-offs in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey seeks $750-800 million of sell-offs in Jan.

text.p: Turkey will prepare at least $750-$800 million worth of sell-offs during January, State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said on Thursday.
"This month privatisations worth at least $750-$800 million will be made ready to be presented to the OYK (High Board of Privatisation)," Soylemez said at a discussion meeting on privatisation.
He added that if the conditions were right it would be possible for the total to be as high as $1 billion.
"The first month of 1997 will be the month when the most privatisation is achieved," he said.
The government's 10-year-old privatisation programme has previously moved along at a sluggish pace because of legal and parliamentary obstacles, raising just over $3 billion since its inception.

The Islamist-conservative coalition established last June by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has targeted an acceleration of the sell-off programme as the key to combating the country's considerable deficit problems.

Erbakan said on Wednesday the 1996 budget deficit would be 1,200 trillion lira, compared with 316.6 trillion a year earlier. Parliament last month approved for 1997 a zero-deficit budget which programmes in considerable sell-off revenues.
State telecommunications company Turk Telekom is the centrepiece of the sell-off programme and progress in pushing ahead with its privatisation in 1997 is vital to the government's plans.
The constitutional court is expected to make a ruling next week on a law enabling the company's sale.
